note: Prompt 10 (worker P10B): the drivable rover's geometry and vehicle tuning. Positions are metres in the ROVER BODY FRAME unless named otherwise: origin on the ground under the middle axle (the map object's origin), -Z forward, +X right, +Y up. A pose {position, quat} is that frame in the world: world = position + quat * offset. Geometry was measured from the map mesh headlessly (tools/godot/rover_drive_check.gd -- --inspect reprints it). Numbers under 'tuning' are fictional game tuning (category game_tuning), chosen for a stable, kid-friendly vehicle under Mars gravity; they are not NASA rover specifications.
choice_evidence: sf_rover (Exterior, 74 604 triangles) is parked inside sf_print_garage: same rotation, origin 0.3 m from the garage origin. The garage's open side (posts at local x +-2.7, 3.8 m clear opening, colliders.json) faces the rover's front, so it drives straight out onto the open ground.

sf_rover has six tyres (material 'rubber': three per side at mesh z -1.55, 0, +1.55; x +-1.1..1.5; radius 0.525 m) and a hollow cabin: floor y 0.88, ceiling y ~2.75, inner half-width 1.15 m, 4.8 m long, with no seat geometry inside (ray probes).
hb_rover (Hangar, 2.2 m wide) stands inside the pressurised hangar whose doors are personnel doors (widest pair 1.36 m, door 2), so it cannot reach the exterior; it has two webbing seats only.

The windows (material sf_win) use the opaque colony_surface shader with back-face culling: from inside, the walls at window height are not drawn, so a seated driver sees out; from outside the cabin is opaque and seated crew are hidden.
mesh_note: The map mesh's authored front is its +Z (headlights at mesh z 1.45..2.43, windscreen to z 2.38, rear step and grate at z -3.05..-2.45). The body frame faces -Z, so the drawn copy is turned 180 degrees about Y.
wheel_note: Six wheels, all driven; the front pair steers and the rear pair counter-steers (steer +1 / -1), the middle pair is fixed; the steered wheels point at one turn centre on the middle axle line (Ackermann), so full lock (30 degrees on the centre line) turns the rover on a 2.7 m radius. The tyres are part of the single map mesh, so they cannot spin or move with the suspension on screen.
collision_note: colliders.json boxes of sf_rover turned into the body frame. The wheel block is raised to start 0.42 m above the ground (the authored box reaches the ground), so the wheels' ray suspension carries the rover and only obstacles taller than 0.42 m strike the body between the wheels.
seat_note: No seats are modelled in the cabin. Four seat anchors stand on the cabin floor, two rows of two (driver front left). Each anchor is where a seated body's feet-level origin goes: the rig's 'seated' clip puts the hips 0.50 m above it (authored for a 0.45 m seat), the head bone 1.11 m and the eyes about 1.29 m above it. The seated legs splay: toe bones reach +-0.54 m to the side and 0.39 m forward.
exit_note: Feet positions on the ground, tried in this order; the first whose standing capsule (0.22 m radius, 1.8 m tall) is clear and has ground under it is used. Parked in the garage the rear hatch faces the garage's back wall and is blocked, so crew leave by the left side.
cargo_note: The cabin behind the rear seats (z 0.9..2.4) up to the rear wall; items loaded into the bay travel with the rover's pose.
enter_note: Largest distance from the pose origin at which a character can still touch the rover: half its length (3.1 m) plus the 2.6 m interaction reach. A host distance check against the pose origin should use this, not interact_distance_m.
garage_clear_note: Body-frame box of the parked rover from 0.12 m above its wheels' ground up to 3 m. The garage mesh has a black floor object (a cable or hose, mesh 'black', up to 0.91 m high, garage local x 0.98..2.52, z -1.82..-0.28) under the parked rover's left rear wheels; as part of the garage's prop trimesh it held the rover in place. The presenter drops the garage trimesh triangles inside this box at load (the pad floor below 0.12 m stays).
garage_park_note: The map placement of sf_rover (Blender (8.3, -23.0, -0.00136), rotated 90 degrees about Z), as the body frame: facing world +X, out of the garage opening (garage front wall at world x 11.5, back wall inner face x 5.0, side walls' inner faces z 20.0 and 26.0).

tuning.note: sag: static spring compression (sets the spring rate from the actual mass, natural frequency sqrt(g/sag) = 1.3 Hz under 3.73 m/s2). centre_of_mass: kept low (batteries in the floor) so the static stability factor is 1.3/0.55 = 2.4, far above the friction-limited lateral acceleration. crew_mass_kg: one suited crew member (game value, not a cited suit mass). Braking is limited by tyre friction (traction_mu x normal load), so under Mars gravity stopping takes longer than on Earth.
